messages.subject: Re: Help With the Inputs
parts:
Hello Barkatullah

I think it is poor practice to perform an elaborate analysis of such meagre data. However, I appreciate this is an opportunity for you to learn about the methods, so I'll restrain my scepticism. I won't answer your question about time varying covariates - that is a fancy twist that is often unnecessary even for much larger datasets.

There are several ways to constrain a mask and include covariates. Here is one; replace names as appropriate. You will need the rgdal package.
datadir <- [your folder with shapefile]
# read polygon shapefile as SpatialPolygonsDataFrame object
SPDF <- rgdal::readOGR(dsn = paste0(datadir, "/habitat.shp"))
tr <- traps(snowleopardCH)
msk <- make.mask(tr, buffer = 10000)  # or whatever buffer you choose
msk <- addCovariates(msk, SPDF)       # look up mask covariates in SPDF
msk <- subset(msk, covariates(msk)$Habitat == 1)  # retain only those mask points with Habitat = 1

plot(msk)
plot(tr, add = TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: Help With the Inputs
parts:
To get reliable results you need to collect more data (or perhaps study a different species!). The packages you mention are all capable of performing a basic SECR analysis, so use the one you know. In my (biased) opinion 'secr' is the most appropriate, but it ultimately makes no difference.
